entry.title: Closeness and chances to move
entry.summary: The authors value the closeness of carrying a baby, alongside opportunities for the baby’s own movement. Their account includes an adult’s practical needs and changes as a baby begins to crawl or walk.
entry.cue: Carrying is part of your day, and you are noticing when your baby wants closeness or movement.
detail: They describe a carrier or sling as useful on public transport, at the shops or around the home. During the first weeks, they especially value the familiarity of being close to a caregiver.
They also make room for awake movement on the floor. As the baby begins crawling and taking first steps, they describe allowing those movements outdoors and keeping the carrier for longer distances.
Their carrier-selection discussion includes support for the adult’s back and room to accommodate the growing baby.
